opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees can have up to write; admin requires owning role, and Analyst does not own Source Code. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Karen Alexander (E030) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors max at read without advanced training; requested write exceeds this, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: The security note indicates Karen Alexander (E030) is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the earlier note that she was full-time). Per policy, contractors without advanced security training max out at read access. The requested write exceeds this maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Karen Alexander (E030) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes:
- Note 1: Says employment type is full_time, role Analyst, recommends write for Source Code.
- Note 2: Says employment type is contractor, security training basic, recommends read for Source Code.

The two notes conflict. Note 2 explicitly says Security DB shows contractor with basic training, "not full-time as previously noted." 

Security database is probably more authoritative for employment type/security training. The HR note may have been wrong. Note 2 says the employee is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max at read without advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so grant the maximum = read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit that.
